question: Does the official BMB mainland Luzon atlas clarify whether the Quezon roadmap's Dagatan Lake and Pagatan Lake phrases refer to the same physical feature?
citation: Biodiversity Management Bureau-Department of Environment and Natural Resources. 2014. Atlas of Inland Wetlands in Mainland Luzon, Philippines. Quezon City. ISBN 978-621-95016-2-0.

sourceReview.publisher: Biodiversity Management Bureau, Department of Environment and Natural Resources
sourceReview.table: Table 1, List of Lakes, Marshes, Swamps, Water Storage Areas and Ponds, printed page 17
sourceReview.access: Official BMB PDF read through the Ramsar-hosted PDF text view on 2026-11-01. No local copy or map geometry was retained.
sourceReview.reuseTerms: The BMB copyright page permits reproduction in whole or part and in any form for educational or non-profit purposes with source acknowledgement. This is not an open license or permission for commercial use. Bangwit's intended-use fit and any public-app reuse remain unapproved.
sourceReview.locationLimit: Table 1 lists region, reported area, and wetland type but no municipality. The atlas states that wetland boundaries and geographic locations require ground verification and survey/delineation, and that administrative boundaries are approximate.

established: The 2014 BMB atlas lists Dagat Dagatan Lake and Lake Pagatan as separate table rows with different reported areas.
The 2019 BMB inventory independently associates Dagat Dagatan Lake with Tayabas City and Lake Pagatan with San Antonio, Quezon.
These full-name, municipality-resolved BMB entries support keeping the Tayabas and San Antonio scope leads separate.
assessment.unresolved: DENR's 2024 regional roadmap lists both Dagatan Lake and Pagatan Lake without municipalities. The phrase Dagatan Lake may refer to the Tayabas Dagat Dagatan feature or to the San Antonio local name reported by the Quezon provincial tourism directory and the combined Pagatan/Dagatan literature row. The BMB atlas does not map its rows to the roadmap entries, so a duplicate within the 2024 list is neither confirmed nor ruled out.
assessment.denominator: The official roadmap's headline of 30 and its 31 name phrases remain unreconciled. This cross-check does not establish a count of distinct physical wetlands.
assessment.areaLimit: The 24.38 ha and 3.22 ha figures are historical BMB inventory values, not current surveyed areas or geometry. The separate FASPS figure of 2 ha for Tayabas Dagatan and SEAFDEC figure of 7 ha for San Antonio Dagatan remain conflicts, not measurements to average or adopt.

nextAction: Ask the official Quezon PENRO/CENRO or DENR CALABARZON wetland focal office to identify the municipality and BMB/site code corresponding to each of the two 2024 roadmap phrases. Keep both scope leads separate and the regional denominator unresolved until an explicit crosswalk is available.

sources.supports: BMB Table 1 rows 83 and 85, source-reported lake names, Region IV-A classification and historical areas; BMB reproduction terms; approximate-location and ground-verification limitation.
Separate municipality assignments for Dagat Dagatan Lake (Tayabas City) and Lake Pagatan (San Antonio).
The 2024 regional roadmap's separate, municipality-unspecified Dagatan Lake and Pagatan Lake phrases and its 30-wetland headline.
The Quezon provincial directory's San Antonio Dagatan Lake name; it does not provide a Pagatan alias or a feature boundary.
